title: Schrag2026Pediatric: pediatric SSVEP-BCI dataset in children and adolescents
description: A pediatric steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) brain-computer interface dataset from 47 healthy, BCI-naive children and adolescents aged 5-18. Participants completed a stimulus personalization and comfort-rating procedure, then played an online four-target SSVEP-controlled game with both a personalized and a standard high-contrast stimulus. EEG was recorded from 16 channels at 256 Hz, with fbCCA classifier outputs used for online control. Note that only 12 trials per game session are ground-truth target events; the labels of the remaining trials are fbCCA classifier outputs rather than ground truth.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a g.tec g.USBamp and g.GAMMAcap (16 active Ag/AgCl wet electrodes, 256 Hz, earlobe reference, Fpz ground). Each participant first completed a personalization stage of 12 stimuli at 10 Hz (5 s on, 5 s baseline, pairwise comfort ratings). Each then played an online 4-target SSVEP game twice, once with a personal stimulus and once with a standard stimulus, using targets at 6.25, 10, 11.11 and 14.28 Hz. Stimuli were presented with Unity3D and BCI-Essentials, and fbCCA was used for classification.
